Bonbons Sirop

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Makes about 24 bonbonsPrep 15 minCook 15 min

Bonbons Sirop are traditional Haitian syrup candies enjoyed during Fête de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa. This sweet treat honors Papa Zaka, the loa of agriculture and harvest, symbolizing the sweetness of the earth's bounty. These sticky, flavored syrup bonbons are a festive favorite among families celebrating the season of planting and harvest.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups granulated sugar (400 g)
  • 1 cup water (240 ml)
  • 1/2 cup light corn syrup (120 ml)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice (15 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract (5 ml)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • Powdered sugar for dusting

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine sugar, water, corn syrup, lime juice, and salt.
  2. Place the saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves completely.
  3. Attach a candy thermometer to the saucepan and bring the mixture to a boil without stirring.
  4. Cook the syrup until it reaches the hard ball stage, about 250°F (121°C).
  5. Remove the saucepan from heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
  6. Pour the hot syrup onto a greased or parchment-lined baking sheet in small spoonfuls or use a candy mold to shape the bonbons.
  7. Allow the syrup to cool and harden completely at room temperature, about 1 hour.
  8. Once set, dust the bonbons lightly with powdered sugar to prevent sticking.
  9. Store the bonbons in an airtight container at room temperature until ready to serve.

Tips

  • Use a candy thermometer for precise temperature control to achieve the perfect hard ball stage.
  • Add a few drops of food coloring or different flavor extracts like anise or coconut for variation.
  • If the syrup is too sticky after cooling, dust generously with powdered sugar or cornstarch to handle easily.
